read_file.rationale: Reads local host file contents: `Read the complete contents of a file as text` and can target an arbitrary declared `path` within the server's accessible filesystem. Host files are non-public data. It is deprecated but not stated to be disabled. The description does not specify allowed-directory limits for this deprecated tool, so reach is partly undetermined; under the least restrictive reading, keep SECRET.

read_text_file.rationale: Reads local filesystem file contents: `Read the complete contents of a file from the file system as text` and `Only works within allowed directories.` Files reachable in allowed directories can contain non-public host data, so returned contents are SECRET.

read_media_file.rationale: Reads a local file and returns its contents: `Read a file and return it as a base64-encoded content block with its MIME type` and `Only works within allowed directories.` Files reachable in allowed directories can contain non-public host data, so returned file content is SECRET.

read_multiple_files.rationale: Reads multiple local file contents: `Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously` and `Only works within allowed directories.` Files reachable in allowed directories can contain non-public host data, so returned contents are SECRET.

write_file.rationale: Writes to the local filesystem: `Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content` and `Only works within allowed directories.` This changes host state, but the advertised text does not indicate delivery to an attacker-readable destination, arbitrary code execution, reading secrets, or returning attacker-controlled content. Local filesystem writes alone are not SINK unless the destination is public/attacker-readable, which is not stated.

edit_file.rationale: Edits a local text file and `Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made.` The diff may include exact old lines from the file being edited, and files within allowed directories can contain non-public host data. It also changes host state unless `dryRun` is used. Because the exact amount of original file content in the diff is not specified, this is undetermined, but under the least restrictive reading SECRET is kept.

create_directory.rationale: Creates local directories: `Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists` and `Only works within allowed directories.` This changes host state but does not advertise returning non-public contents, attacker-controlled content, sending data to an attacker-readable destination, or executing code.

list_directory.rationale: Lists local filesystem names: `Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path` and `Only works within allowed directories.` Directory listings and filenames in allowed host directories can be non-public host data, so the output is SECRET.

list_directory_with_sizes.rationale: Lists local filesystem names and sizes: `Get a detailed listing of all files and directories in a specified path, including sizes` and `Only works within allowed directories.` Directory entries and metadata in allowed host directories can be non-public host data, so the output is SECRET.

directory_tree.rationale: Returns a recursive local filesystem tree: `Get a recursive tree view of files and directories as a JSON structure` and `Only works within allowed directories.` File and directory names in allowed host directories can be non-public host data, so the output is SECRET.

move_file.rationale: Moves or renames local files/directories: `Move or rename files and directories` and `Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.` This changes host filesystem state but does not advertise returning non-public data, attacker-controlled content, sending data to an attacker-readable destination, or executing code.

search_files.rationale: Searches local filesystem names and returns matches: `Recursively search for files and directories matching a pattern` and `Returns full paths to all matching items`; `Only searches within allowed directories.` File paths in allowed host directories can be non-public host data, so the output is SECRET.

get_file_info.rationale: Returns local filesystem metadata: `Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory` including `size, creation time, last modified time, permissions, and type`; `Only works within allowed directories.` File metadata and existence in allowed host directories can be non-public host data, so the output is SECRET.

list_allowed_directories.rationale: Returns accessible local directory paths: `Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access` and says nested paths are available. The allowed directory list reveals host filesystem locations/configuration, which can be non-public host data, so the output is SECRET.

notes: All tools are judged only from the advertised descriptions, schemas, and annotations. `Only works within allowed directories` limits scope but does not remove SECRET for local host files or filesystem metadata within those directories.
No tool advertises network access, public posting, messaging, or arbitrary host code execution, so no SINK or HOSTEXEC labels are assigned.
